content: The book Welfare, Choice and Solidarity in Transition: Reforming the Health Sector in Eastern Europe, authored by János Kornai and Karen Eggleston, was published in 2001. It examines the health sector reforms in ten post-socialist countries in Eastern Europe, specifically Albania, Bulgaria, Croatia, the Czech Republic, Hungary, the Republic of Macedonia, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. By 2007, based on the World Bank's classification, Albania was categorized as a lower-middle-income economy. In contrast, the Czech Republic and Slovenia were classified as high-income economies, while the remaining countries were considered upper-middle-income economies.
